headline: Nvidia's Huang returns, stocks have best day since April 2025
summary: US stocks surged on Monday after Nvidia brought back CEO Jensen Huang, following pressure from President Trump. The [[S&P 500]] rose 4.73% to 7237.17 and the [[Nasdaq]] rose 6.51%, the best day since April 2025. The [[VIX]], a gauge of how big a swing traders expect, fell 25.83% to 26.62, so fear eased fast. Nvidia is so large that its mood steers the whole [[index]], and it rose 30% or more. Bond moves were small (the 10-year [[yield]] rose 1 [[basis point]]), so this was an AI and stocks story, not a rates story.
one_thing: One company's CEO news lifted the S&P 500 by 4.73% in a day, which shows how much the market now leans on the AI trade. Meanwhile the Fed still says higher rates are likely, so the rebound sits on shaky ground.

cross_asset.stocks: The Nasdaq (+6.51%) beat the S&P 500 (+4.73%), which beat the Dow (+3.01%). That order shows the money chased tech and AI first. Consumer stocks such as Kroger and Tyson fell, which suggests investors sold their [[defensive stocks]] to buy AI. Oracle and CoreWeave also jumped because Nvidia's financing keeps the AI cloud firms funded.
cross_asset.rates: The 10-year yield rose 1 bp to 4.92%, which is a tiny move. The 2-year yield is 4.63%, so the [[yield curve]] (10-year minus 2-year) is +29 bp. Last week yields fell as AI worries sent investors into safer bonds. Today that safe-haven demand eased, yet yields barely moved. That suggests the Fed matters more than AI for bonds right now, since Fed's John Williams said higher rates are likely 'over time'.
cross_asset.fx: The dollar index rose 0.49% to 104.32. Headlines tie the dollar rally to bets on a hawkish Fed, and Goldman Sachs expects it to continue before a pullback in 2027. It also warns that the dollar looks overbought. USD/JPY fell 0.47% to 158.96, so the yen gained even as the dollar rose. The headlines do not explain the yen move, so the cause is unclear.
cross_asset.commodities: WTI crude fell 4.29% to 80.38, its lowest settle since August. Oil kept flowing out of the Persian Gulf despite attacks on ships, so traders worried less about a shortage. Gold rose 3.26% to 3629.9 even though stocks soared. Gold usually gains on fear, so the cause of this gain is unclear.

storylines.name: AI trade jitters
storylines.backstory: Markets leaned on the biggest AI-linked tech firms, so doubts about AI hit the whole index. Nvidia's CEO left on Nov 12 and a selloff followed. Official papers warned that AI [[valuation]]s look stretched, and the S&P 500 fell four straight weeks.
storylines.today: Nvidia's board approved Huang's return and Reuters says Trump pressured the company to do it. The stock rose 30% or more and the S&P 500 had its best day since April 2025. The cheering came with pushback. Members of both parties in Congress questioned Trump's view that Huang is not a national security risk. Treasury Secretary Bessent reversed his harder line on Nvidia. Staff allegations of workplace abuse surfaced, and one headline mentions a reported SEC probe. A strategist warned that Wall Street is not pricing in a data center slowdown. HPE posted its strongest growth ever but its stock wavered, which shows even good AI news does not lift everything.
storylines.market_link: Huang returns, so Nvidia jumps. Nvidia is a huge share of the index, so the index jumps. A rising index means traders expect less turbulence, so the VIX falls (it dropped 25.83%). Nvidia also finances AI cloud firms like Oracle and CoreWeave, so its rebound makes their funding look safer, which helps their stocks and their [[credit spread]]s. Money also left defensive stocks, so consumer names fell.
storylines.next_chapter: Watch for Congress or the SEC turning the criticism into real action. Also watch whether Nvidia holds its gains without a day of profit-taking. Analysts are split on whether this is a bottom or a short rebound.
storylines.note:
S&P 500 +4.73%, Nasdaq +6.51%, VIX -25.83% to 26.62.
Nvidia is so big that one CEO headline moved the whole index.
Interview line: 'Today's rally was concentrated in AI, so it is a sentiment rebound, not proof the valuation worries are gone.'

storylines.name: Central banks vs energy inflation
storylines.backstory: The Iran war cut oil supply and pushed up headline inflation. Central banks must decide whether the price jump fades or leaks into wages and services. Euro area inflation hit 4%, the Bank of England hiked to 4%, and the Fed sits at 3.875%.
storylines.today: Fed's John Williams said higher interest rates are likely 'over time' to address inflation. He also said he is confident inflation gets closer to 2% in 2027. Waller said the Fed meets Dec 8 and 9. Cook said damaged infrastructure and low inventories could keep oil prices high for a long time. Japan's core inflation hit its highest this year as an energy subsidy ended. Friday's note said FTSE futures slipped on a hawkish read of US rates. The 2-year yield is 4.63%, above the Fed's 3.875% rate, so markets already price some hikes.
storylines.market_link: Oil rises, so fuel and shipping costs rise, so headline inflation rises. The Fed then leans toward a [[rate hike]]. Expected hikes push the 2-year yield up first, and that pulls the dollar up. A San Francisco Fed paper adds a twist. When inflation comes from supply shocks like oil, Fed surprises move longer-term yields less than when demand is the cause.
storylines.next_chapter: The Dec 8 and 9 Fed meeting is the big test. Before it, watch the GDP and personal income data this week. Also watch whether oil's drop to its lowest settle since August eases pressure on the hawks.
storylines.note:
Fed 3.875%, BoE 4.0%, ECB 2.5%, BOJ 1.25%.
Williams: higher rates likely over time, inflation near 2% in 2027.
Interview line: 'Supply-driven inflation is harder for central banks because hiking does not fix a shortage.'

storylines.name: Iran war and oil
storylines.backstory: The conflict began in early 2026 and cut global oil output by 12 mb/d in March. Prices jumped but not to records, because stored oil filled the gap. Tensions eased in June and then returned. The IEA says the Hormuz shock lifted the world's oil and gas import bill 25% to $1.6 trillion.
storylines.today: WTI fell 4.29% to 80.38, its lowest settle since August. Oil kept flowing out of the Persian Gulf even though tanker attacks continue. Another headline says China has become the top oil buyer. Earlier this week Trump suggested recent gas price drops are tied to the election, calling it 'a giant hoax' in one headline. The Bank of Japan's speech noted that oil is below its April peak but still fairly high.
storylines.market_link: Oil flows continue, so traders worry less about a shortage, so crude falls. Cheaper crude means cheaper gasoline and diesel, which helps drivers and delivery firms. Lower fuel costs trim headline inflation, so the Fed feels slightly less pressure. The war is not over, so one attack could reverse this fast.
storylines.next_chapter: Watch for new tanker attacks or a Gulf disruption, which would send oil up again. Also watch whether the price stays below where it was in August. Cook warns that damaged infrastructure and low inventories can keep prices high for a long time.
storylines.note:
WTI 80.38, -4.29%, lowest settle since August.
Oil down means less pressure on headline inflation and on the Fed.
Interview line: 'Oil is falling on flows, not on peace, so the risk is still two-sided.'

storylines.name: US midterms and the dollar
storylines.backstory: The midterms produced what headlines call a Democratic rout. Markets asked how divided government might change tariffs, spending and the dollar. The dollar then had its biggest rally since 2024.
storylines.today: The dollar index rose 0.49% to 104.32. Headlines credit hawkish Fed bets, not the election. Goldman Sachs expects the rally to continue in the coming months and fade in 2027. Its technical read says the dollar is overbought and could slow. Sterling and the euro edged up in the morning as the stock rebound took some shine off the dollar. By the close the dollar was higher again.
storylines.market_link: Traders expect the Fed to hold rates high or raise them. Higher US rates make dollar deposits pay more, so investors buy dollars. A stronger dollar makes imports cheaper for Americans but makes dollar debts harder for other countries. Usually a risk-on day weakens the dollar. Today both rose, which shows Fed bets are the stronger force.
storylines.next_chapter: Watch for the dollar falling when Fed odds soften. Also watch whether the overbought warning turns into a real pullback. For the yen, watch the Bank of Japan, since USD/JPY is near 159.
storylines.note:
Dollar index 104.32 (+0.49%), USD/JPY 158.96 (-0.47%).
Hawkish Fed means higher US rates, which means a stronger dollar.
Interview line: 'The dollar is trading the Fed, not the election.'

stories.title: Best stock day since April 2025 came from one CEO
stories.what: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang and the S&P 500 rose 4.73%. The Nasdaq gained 6.51% and the Dow 3.01%. The VIX fell 25.83% to 26.62.
stories.why: Think of Nvidia like the lead singer of a band that everyone came to see. When the singer quits, ticket sales drop. When the singer returns, they jump. A market that relies this much on a few firms is exposed if the leader's story changes again.
stories.watch: Watch for Nvidia and the Nasdaq giving back part of the gain. Last week's loss was recovered by just over half, so a lot of ground is left to make up.

stories.title: Williams says higher rates are likely over time
stories.what: Fed's John Williams said higher rates are likely 'over time' to address inflation. He expects inflation to move closer to the 2% target in 2027. Waller said the Fed meets Dec 8 and 9. Fed rate-hike odds jumped on the day.
stories.why: A higher Fed rate means higher rates on mortgages, car loans and credit cards. It also means savings accounts pay more. Williams is an influential voice, so when he leans toward hikes, traders treat it as a signal for the whole committee.
stories.watch: Watch the 2-year yield (4.63%) into the Dec 8 and 9 meeting. A move above 4.92% on the 2-year would flip the curve into a hike-priced shape.

stories.title: Oil falls to its lowest settle since August
stories.what: WTI fell 4.29% to 80.38. Middle East crude kept flowing despite tanker attacks. China became the top oil buyer, according to one headline.
stories.why: Lower oil means cheaper gas and diesel for households and trucking firms. It trims headline inflation, the number that central banks watch. That gives the Fed a bit more room, though Cook still warns about damaged infrastructure and low inventories.
stories.watch: Watch for more tanker attacks. Also watch whether China's buying lifts prices again.

stories.title: Congress and Treasury clash over Huang's return
stories.what: Members of both parties in Congress sharply questioned Trump's view that Huang poses no national security risk. Bessent reversed his harder line on Nvidia. Staff allegations of workplace abuse and a reported SEC probe added to the noise.
stories.why: The market cheered, but the same company is now tied to politics, China policy and legal risk. If Washington pushes back, the rally could lose its main support. Policy risk is hard to price.
stories.watch: Watch for congressional hearings or letters. Also watch for any SEC news.

stories.title: Nvidia's money keeps AI cloud firms alive
stories.what: Oracle and CoreWeave had big gains. Headlines say Nvidia's financing of the AI ecosystem is crucial for firms like Oracle, CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren. St. Louis Fed research shows data center builders lean more on debt than other big tech.
stories.why: A company that depends on loans is like a driver who needs a refill to keep going. If the financier worries, the borrower suffers fast. So Nvidia's health spreads into bond and loan markets.
stories.watch: Watch the borrowing costs of data center builders. Also watch if the rebound makes banks and investors lend more freely.

under_the_radar.title: Fed survey on how banks manage reserves
under_the_radar.what: The Fed released a survey of senior financial officers about how banks manage their reserve balances. The banks in it held about three-fourths of all reserves in the system. Banks were asked about their balance sheet plans, deposits and money market activity.
under_the_radar.chain: Reserves are the cash banks keep at the Fed. If banks want to keep more of it, less cash is lent in short-term markets. That can push short-term borrowing rates up. Those rates feed into how companies and traders fund themselves day to day. The headlines do not give the survey's results, so any effect here is possible but not shown.
under_the_radar.watch: Watch for jumps in short-term funding rates or comments from the Fed about its balance sheet. Either would show this is becoming important.
under_the_radar.note:
Survey covered banks holding about 75% of reserves.
Reserves are the cash banks keep at the Fed.
Interview line: 'Reserve demand sets how smoothly overnight funding markets work.'

under_the_radar.title: US workforce could stop growing
under_the_radar.what: A New York Fed post says US working-age population growth has fallen to near zero because net immigration dropped sharply. The native-born working-age population is also shrinking, so available labor could soon start to shrink.
under_the_radar.chain: Fewer workers means employers compete harder for them, so wages can rise. Higher wages raise the cost of services like haircuts and healthcare. That can keep inflation sticky even after oil falls. A sticky inflation reading would keep the Fed hawkish, which would lift short-term yields and the dollar.
under_the_radar.watch: Watch for wage and services inflation data. Also watch the Fed's own comments about the labor supply.
under_the_radar.note:
US working-age population growth is near zero.
Fewer workers means higher wage pressure, then stickier inflation, then a hawkish Fed.
Interview line: 'Labor supply is a quiet inflation force that does not show up in oil prices.'

under_the_radar.title: ECB lets tokenised assets count as collateral
under_the_radar.what: The ECB will accept assets issued on licensed DLT platforms as eligible collateral for its credit operations. Details are due in spring 2027 and implementation is planned for June 2027. It follows a similar step announced on 27 January 2026.
under_the_radar.chain: Banks must post [[collateral]] to borrow from the ECB. A wider list of assets means more things can be pledged. If tokenised assets become easy to pledge, they may trade like normal bonds. This is a slow plumbing change, so the effect on rates is small for now.
under_the_radar.watch: Watch for the spring 2027 rulebook. The signal that it matters would be large issuers choosing DLT platforms.
under_the_radar.note:
ECB details due spring 2027, start planned for June 2027.
Collateral is what banks pledge to borrow from the central bank.
Interview line: 'Central banks are slowly making tokenised assets usable in the core of the financial system.'

deep_dive.why_now: Nvidia's rebound shows how much markets rely on the AI buildout, so how it is paid for matters. This St. Louis Fed note tells us who is using debt and who is using cash.
key_points: The study looks at 10 big firms, including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Broadcom, Intel, IBM, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Oracle. It calls them hyperscalers.
Their debt relative to assets fell from nearly 30% in 2023 to roughly 25% in early 2026. Other US public firms stayed near 34%.
Their payouts to shareholders fell from about 4% of assets in 2022 to about 2% in early 2026, so they are keeping more cash for investment.
Data center builders lean more on debt and have cut shareholder payouts to fund growth. Chip suppliers cover more modest investment from operating cash flow.
The study leaves out off-balance-sheet commitments like leases and purchase obligations, which may be a big part of data center builders' plans.
deep_dive.market_angle: Credit markets are the main link. The big firms look financially strong, which supports their stocks and bonds. The data center builders look riskier, so their spreads are more sensitive to Nvidia's mood and the AI rebound. If AI enthusiasm fades, those spreads widen first. The Nasdaq would fall.
deep_dive.trade_idea: A desk might hold the strong big-tech names and buy [[credit default swap]] protection on a data center builder. The aim is to profit if the AI mood sours without betting against the whole sector. The main risk is that Nvidia keeps financing the ecosystem and the rally continues, so the protection just costs money.
deep_dive.note:
Hyperscaler debt/assets: nearly 30% (2023) to about 25% (early 2026). Other firms about 34%.
Big AI spenders use cash. Data center builders use debt.
Interview line: 'The AI boom is mostly cash-funded at the top, but the leverage sits further down the chain.'

deep_dive.why_now: Oil-driven inflation is the main worry for central banks, and the Fed meets Dec 8 and 9. This paper explains why the cause of inflation changes how markets react.
key_points: The Fed tends to respond more aggressively to demand-driven inflation than to supply-driven inflation.
The authors study policy surprises, which are the unexpected part of Fed announcements, and how they move forward rates.
Surprises mostly pass through to longer-horizon rates when inflation is demand-driven.
Supply-side pressures like energy have grown since the pandemic, so Fed surprises are likely to move long yields less.
The method treats price and quantity moving in the same direction as demand, and in opposite directions as supply.
deep_dive.market_angle: The curve is the main market. If the Fed surprises hawkishly while inflation comes from supply, the 2-year yield should rise more than the 10-year yield. That would flatten the 10-year minus 2-year curve from +29 bp. The dollar would probably gain as well.
deep_dive.trade_idea: A desk might consider a 2s10s [[flattener]], which means betting the gap between the 10-year and 2-year yield shrinks. The main risk is that inflation leaks into wages and the market doubts the Fed. Then long yields could rise too and the curve would steepen.
deep_dive.note:
Supply-driven inflation moves long yields less than demand-driven inflation.
Hawkish Fed surprise means 2Y up more than 10Y, so the curve flattens from +29 bp.
Interview line: 'The source of inflation changes how far the Fed's words travel along the curve.'
deep_dive.title: When Is Monetary Policy Transmission Strongest?

watch_next.why: Waller said officials present their outlook on Dec 8 and their policy view on Dec 9. After Williams' comment, traders will look for any sign of a hike.
A headline says the dollar was focused on these reports. Strong numbers could add to hawkish Fed bets and lift yields.

watch_next.why: Bipartisan criticism and a reported SEC probe could weaken the AI rally if they turn into action.

watch_next.event: Persian Gulf tanker flows and attacks
watch_next.why: Oil fell to its lowest settle since August because flows continued. A disruption would reverse that fast and add to inflation worries.

watch_next.event: Bank of Japan rate hike signal
watch_next.why: The BOJ chief signaled a near-term hike. A hike would narrow the gap to the Fed's 3.875% and could help the yen, which sits near 159 per dollar.

terms.def: The VIX is a gauge of how big a stock move traders expect, like a weather forecast for storms in the market.
The yield curve compares short-term and long-term interest rates, like checking whether a loan costs more for one year or ten.
Supply-driven inflation comes from shortages like less oil, so it is like a price jump caused by a closed road rather than by shoppers spending more.
A hyperscaler is a giant tech firm that builds huge data centers and chips, like a landlord for the internet's computing power.
Overbought means a price has risen so fast it may need a rest, like a runner who sprinted the first mile.
Risk-on describes days when investors feel brave and buy stocks, like people going out because the weather is clear.

cross_asset_notes: S&P 500 7237.17 (+4.73%), Nasdaq 24089.56 (+6.51%): tech led, so this was an AI rebound, not a broad boom.
VIX 26.62 (-25.83%): fear fell fast, but 26.62 is still an elevated level, so nerves are not gone.
10Y 4.92% (+1 bp), 2Y 4.63%, curve +29 bp: bonds barely moved, so the Fed is the main driver of rates.
WTI 80.38 (-4.29%), lowest settle since August: cheaper oil eases inflation worries, but gold +3.26% to 3629.9 has no clear cause.
take: The VIX fell 25.83% to 26.62 in one day, while the Fed's Williams says higher rates are likely 'over time'. Make a call on the VIX into the Dec 8 and 9 Fed meeting. Would you bet that it stays below 26.62, or that it rises back above it? Explain why, and say what single piece of news would prove you wrong.

Nasdaq.def: The Nasdaq is an index that tracks a big group of stocks, and it leans heavily toward tech companies. When tech jumps or falls, the Nasdaq moves the most.
Nasdaq.analogy: It is like a school report card that counts the science classes much more than the art classes.
Nasdaq.today: The Nasdaq rose 6.51% to 24089.56, the biggest gain among the major US indexes, because Nvidia's rebound lifted tech first.

S&P 500.def: The S&P 500 is an index of 500 large US companies. It is the most common way to ask 'how is the US stock market doing?'
S&P 500.analogy: It is like the average grade of the 500 biggest students in a school.
S&P 500.today: The S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7237.17, its best day since April 2025, after Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia.

VIX.def: The VIX is a number that shows how big a swing in US stocks traders expect over the next month. A high VIX means traders are nervous and a low VIX means they feel calm.
VIX.analogy: It is like a storm forecast for the market. A high number means traders expect heavy weather.
VIX.today: The VIX fell 25.83% to 26.62, so fear eased fast. The level is still elevated, which means nerves have not fully gone.

basis point.def: A basis point is one hundredth of one percentage point. Traders use it to talk about small changes in interest rates.
basis point.analogy: It is like measuring a short walk in steps instead of miles.
basis point.today: The 10-year yield rose 1 basis point to 4.92%, which is a tiny move even on a huge stock day.

collateral.def: Collateral is something valuable you hand over to a lender as a promise you will repay. If you do not repay, the lender keeps it.
collateral.analogy: It is like leaving your bike with a friend when you borrow their laptop.
collateral.today: The ECB said it will accept assets issued on licensed DLT platforms as collateral. Details are due in spring 2027 and the change starts in June 2027.

credit default swap.def: A credit default swap is an insurance contract against a borrower failing to pay its debt. The buyer pays a regular fee and gets paid if the borrower defaults.
credit default swap.analogy: It is like car insurance for a loan. You pay a small fee each month in case of a crash.
credit default swap.today: The deep dive suggested a desk could buy this protection on a data center builder, since those firms lean more on debt than the biggest tech firms.

credit spread.def: A credit spread is the extra interest a company must pay over a very safe borrower like the US government. A wider spread means investors see more risk.
credit spread.analogy: It is like a risk fee that a shaky borrower pays on top of the normal price of a loan.
credit spread.today: Nvidia's rebound made the funding of AI cloud firms like Oracle and CoreWeave look safer, which tends to narrow their spreads.

defensive stocks.def: Defensive stocks are shares of companies people keep paying for in bad times, such as groceries and food makers. They tend to fall less when the market drops.
defensive stocks.analogy: They are like a winter coat. You do not need it on sunny days, but you hold it for storms.
defensive stocks.today: Kroger and Tyson Foods were among the S&P 500's biggest losers because investors sold safer names to buy AI stocks.

flattener.def: A flattener is a trade that wins when the gap between long-term and short-term interest rates gets smaller. A 2s10s flattener uses the 2-year and 10-year yields.
flattener.analogy: It is like betting that a steep hill will turn into a gentle slope.
flattener.today: The 10-year minus 2-year gap is +29 bp. The deep dive suggested a desk might bet on that gap shrinking if the Fed surprises while oil drives inflation.

index.def: An index is a basket of stocks combined into one number. It shows how a whole market or group of companies is doing.
index.analogy: It is like a fruit basket price. You track the basket instead of each apple.
index.today: Nvidia is so large inside the S&P 500 and Nasdaq that one CEO headline moved both indexes by several percent.

rate hike.def: A rate hike is when a central bank raises its main interest rate. This makes borrowing cost more and makes saving pay more.
rate hike.analogy: It is like a school raising the late fee on library books to change behavior.
rate hike.today: Fed official John Williams said higher rates are likely 'over time', and headlines said hike odds jumped. The Fed rate is 3.875% and it meets Dec 8 and 9.

valuation.def: Valuation is how expensive a stock or market is compared with the profits it earns. A high valuation means investors are paying a lot for each dollar of profit.
valuation.analogy: It is like paying 50 dollars for a lemonade stand that earns 1 dollar a day.
valuation.today: Earlier official papers warned AI valuations look stretched. A strategist said the market is not pricing in a data center slowdown, so the worry is still open.

yield.def: A yield is the yearly return you earn from holding a bond, shown as a percentage. It moves in the opposite direction to the bond's price.
yield.analogy: It is like the interest rate on a loan you make to the government.
yield.today: The 10-year yield rose 1 bp to 4.92% and the 2-year yield is 4.63%. Bonds barely reacted to the stock surge.

yield curve.def: The yield curve compares interest rates on short loans and long loans to the government. Its shape can hint at what traders expect from the economy and the Fed.
yield curve.analogy: It is like checking whether a one-year loan costs more or less than a ten-year loan.
yield curve.today: The 10-year minus 2-year gap is +29 bp, so long-term yields are higher than short-term yields.

steps.label: 10-year yield edges up
steps.explain: The 10-year [[yield]] rose 1 [[basis point]] to 4.92%, which is a tiny move.
steps.detail: Last week yields fell as AI worries sent investors into safer bonds. Today that safe-haven buying eased, but hike talk held yields up. So the Fed mattered more for bonds than the AI rebound.

steps.label: Dollar gains
steps.explain: Higher expected US rates make dollar deposits pay more, so the dollar index rose 0.49% to 104.32.
steps.detail: A risk-on day usually weakens the dollar, so today's rise shows Fed bets were the stronger force. Goldman Sachs expects the rally to continue, then fade in 2027. It also warns the dollar looks overbought.

steps.label: Gulf oil keeps flowing
steps.explain: Crude kept moving out of the Persian Gulf even though attacks on ships continue.
steps.detail: The Iran war cut global oil output by 12 mb/d in March, but flows have returned. A Libyan pipeline restart added supply earlier. The war is not over, so this can change fast.

steps.label: Shortage fears ease
steps.explain: When oil keeps arriving, traders worry less that buyers will run out.
steps.detail: China also became the top oil buyer, according to one headline. The market is trading on flows, not on peace. Fed Governor Cook still warns that damaged infrastructure and low inventories could keep prices high for a long time.

steps.label: WTI falls
steps.explain: WTI crude fell 4.29% to 80.38, its lowest settle since August.
steps.detail: A lower price means sellers must accept less for each barrel. This extends the drop from the 80.92 level of the previous debrief. Oil is still well above where it was before the war, so the move is a retreat, not a collapse.

steps.label: Fuel gets cheaper
steps.explain: Cheaper crude means cheaper gasoline and diesel for drivers and delivery firms.
steps.detail: Lower fuel costs trim headline inflation, the number central banks watch most closely. That gives the Fed a little less pressure, though Williams still leans toward higher rates. One attack on a tanker could reverse the move.

quiz.q: The Nasdaq rose 6.51% while the Dow rose only 3.01%. What best explains the gap?
options: The Fed's Williams hinted at lower rates for tech
Money chased tech and AI first after Huang's return
Investors sold tech to buy the Dow's steadier names
Falling oil hurt the industrial firms in the Dow
quiz.explain: The Nasdaq leans toward tech, and Nvidia's jump drove the day. The order Nasdaq, S&P 500, Dow shows money chased AI first.

quiz.q: Last week yields fell on AI worries. Today the S&P 500 rose 4.73% but the 10-year yield rose only 1 bp. What does that suggest?
options: Bond traders were waiting for the ECB's collateral rules
Oil's drop to 80.38 cancelled out the stock rally
Bonds had already priced the full AI rebound last week
Bonds were driven by Fed rate talk more than AI mood
quiz.explain: Safe-haven buying eased, yet yields barely moved. The Fed's hike signals from Williams were the stronger force for bonds.

quiz.q: The Fed surprises with a hike signal while inflation comes mainly from oil. The gap between the 10-year and 2-year yield, now +29 bp, would probably go which way?
options: Up
Down
quiz.explain: The San Francisco Fed paper says surprises pass through less to long yields when inflation is supply-driven. So the 2-year rises more than the 10-year and the gap shrinks.

quiz.q: WTI fell 4.29% to its lowest settle since August because the attacks on tankers stopped.
options: True
False
quiz.explain: Tanker attacks are still happening. Oil fell because crude kept flowing out of the Gulf despite them.

quiz.q: Gold rose 3.26% to 3629.9 while the VIX fell 25.83%. What is the honest reading from today's headlines?
options: The headlines give no cause, so it stays unexplained
Oil's drop to 80.38 pushed buyers into gold instead
A weaker dollar made gold cheaper for foreign buyers
Fear rose in other markets, so buyers hid in gold
quiz.explain: Gold usually gains on fear, but fear fell today. The dollar also rose, so the cheaper-gold story fails. The debrief says the cause is unclear.

quiz.q: Kroger and Tyson fell today as money rushed into AI. If the AI trade wobbles next week, what would these defensive stocks probably do?
options: Up
Down
quiz.explain: Today's selling was a swap out of safe names into AI. If AI wobbles, some money would likely flow back to the safe names.

quiz.q: Put today's stock chain in order, from cause to effect.
quiz.explain: The news lifts Nvidia first. Nvidia's weight in the index lifts the S&P 500, and a calmer market pulls the VIX down.

quiz.q: Put today's oil chain in order, from cause to effect.
items: Gulf oil keeps flowing despite attacks
quiz.explain: Supply keeps arriving, so traders worry less and the price drops. Cheaper fuel then feeds into lower headline inflation.

quiz.q: The 2-year yield of 4.63% sits above the Fed's 3.875% rate, which hints that markets already expect some hikes.
options: True
False
quiz.explain: The 2-year yield tracks expected Fed rates. A yield well above the current rate means traders expect the Fed to raise it.

quiz.q: Williams said higher rates are likely 'over time' but expects inflation near 2% in 2027. What is the best reading?
options: The Fed expects hikes to push inflation higher into 2027
The Fed would hike over time and expect relief by 2027
The Fed sees oil as demand-driven, so the jump will last
The Fed plans cuts soon because inflation is nearly beaten
quiz.explain: He leans toward more hikes now and expects inflation to move closer to the 2% target in 2027. Oil is a supply shock, not a demand one.

quiz.q: The dollar index rose 0.49% to 104.32 on a day the Nasdaq rose 6.51%. Which explanation fits best?
options: Hawkish Fed bets outweighed the usual risk-on dip in the dollar
Japan's intervention forced extra dollar buying by Tokyo today
Fresh midterm election news drove heavy dollar buying today
Goldman's call for a 2027 pullback pulled buyers in today
quiz.explain: Headlines tie the dollar's rally to hawkish Fed bets, not the election. Japan's intervention means selling dollars, so it points the other way.

quiz.q: Members of both parties questioned Trump's view of Huang and Bessent reversed his harder line. Why does this matter for a market that rose 4.73%?
options: Bessent's reversal ends tariffs, which would hit the dollar
Congress sets the Fed's rate, so hikes could follow
The rally leans on one firm, so action could remove it
Any criticism pushes the VIX higher automatically each day
quiz.explain: Today's rally rests heavily on Nvidia's story. Political or legal action, like the reported SEC probe, could remove that support.

quiz.q: Kroger and Tyson were among the S&P 500's biggest losers while Nvidia soared. What does that suggest?
options: Rate hike talk hit only food firms and nobody else
Investors sold safer defensive names to buy AI shares
Shoppers cut grocery spending after the stock rally
Falling oil raised the costs of food producers today
quiz.explain: Consumer stocks were seen as a safe bet during the AI cracks. When AI recovered, money moved out of them and into tech.

quiz.q: A New York Fed post says US working-age population growth is near zero. How could that keep the Fed hawkish even if oil falls?
options: Scarce workers push up wages, so service prices stay sticky
Fewer workers cut oil demand, so oil would rebound
Fewer workers weaken the dollar, so imports cost more
Fewer workers shrink bank reserves, lifting funding costs
quiz.explain: Fewer available workers means employers compete for them and wages can rise. That keeps services inflation sticky even when fuel gets cheaper.

quiz.q: Nvidia's financing of Oracle and CoreWeave suddenly looks shaky. What would the credit spreads on data center builders probably do?
options: Up
Down
quiz.explain: A wider spread is the extra pay lenders demand for more risk. Data center builders lean on debt, so they would feel the worry first.

quiz.q: Before today's drop, the VIX was above 30.
options: True
False
quiz.explain: A fall of 25.83% to 26.62 means the VIX was about 36 yesterday. So fear was high before it eased.
